D019-D018_h001.question:
I’ve been having trouble sleeping ever since… well, since the incident on the flight. It’s not that I can’t fall asleep—I do, at first—but then I wake up gasping, drenched in sweat, like I’m back in the cabin during the turbulence. For a second, I can’t tell if I’m lying in my bed or still strapped in the jumpseat, yelling over the alarms. It only lasts a moment, but it feels real. I check my room, make sure the door’s locked, like maybe that’ll help.  

The flights… they’ve been harder. I go through the motions—smiling, serving drinks, stowing luggage—but sometimes, when the plane drops even a little, my chest tightens and I forget where I am for a second. I’ve snapped back quickly, but it’s embarrassing. I’m supposed to be the calm one, the one passengers look to. Now I dread takeoff.  

I haven’t told anyone at work. I don’t know how long this has been going on—weeks, maybe? Less than a month? More? I stopped counting. I just know I’m not myself. I startle at loud noises, and I keep replaying it, wondering what I could’ve done differently. But is it normal to feel this way after something like that? Or is it too much?
D019-D018_h001.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D019-D018_h001.answer: A & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h002.question:
I’ve just been trying to get through each day, you know? Ever since what happened at the clinic with that dog—the one that was hit by the car—I can’t seem to shake it. I keep seeing it again, like I’m right back there: the blood, the way he was panting, me holding him down while we tried everything. Sometimes I’m brushing a cat in the recovery room and suddenly I’m back in the trauma bay, my gloves are soaked, the vet’s yelling at me to intubate—it feels real, like it’s happening all over again. It only lasts a few seconds, but I lose track of where I am.  

I’ve been sleeping a lot, too much maybe. I get home from my shift and just crash—sleep twelve, fourteen hours straight. I don’t even dream; I just… disappear. On my days off, I don’t get out of bed until afternoon, if at all. It’s not like I feel rested. I just can’t face being awake.  

I haven’t told anyone at work. I’m scared they’ll think I can’t handle it. But I’m barely holding on. I don’t know how long this’s been going—weeks? Less? More? I’ve lost count.
D019-D018_h002.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D019-D018_h002.answer: A & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h003.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time lately—sleep just won’t come, even when I’m exhausted. I lie in bed for hours, mind racing, and every little sound makes me jolt. It’s been like this since… well, since a few weeks ago. There was an incident—I was followed walking home from the lab late at night, nothing “happened,” not really, but I haven’t felt safe since. I keep replaying it, even when I don’t want to. If I hear footsteps behind me now, or see someone in a dark hoodie, my chest tightens and I start shaking. Sometimes just walking past that spot on the sidewalk makes me feel like I can’t breathe.  

I’ve been avoiding that route entirely, which is ridiculous—I’m a researcher, I analyze data, I don’t usually let feelings override logic—but I can’t help it. I’ve also been distracted at work, struggling to focus on my dissertation. My advisor noticed. I don’t want to fall behind, but my mind keeps going back.  

I can’t tell if this is normal stress or something more. It hasn’t been *that* long. Maybe I just need time? But it doesn’t feel like it’s getting better.
D019-D018_h003.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D019-D018_h003.answer: A & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h004.question: I’ve been having a really hard time since it happened. Some nights, I just can’t fall asleep—I lie there for hours, my mind racing like the whole thing is replaying on a loop. When I do drift off, I sometimes wake up gasping, not sure where I am, like I'm right back in that moment. It’s only been a few times, but it feels real—like I’m living through it all over again. I’m the principal at a high school, so I have to be “on” all the time, making decisions, handling crises, staying calm for everyone else. But lately, I’ve been zoning out during meetings, like I’m a million miles away. My husband notices. He says I’ve been jumpy, short-tempered. I don’t want to talk about it, but I can’t stop thinking about it either. It happened not long ago—recent enough that everything still feels raw, but I can’t tell if it’s getting worse or if I’m just noticing it more. I keep wondering… is this normal?     C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D019-D018_h005.question: I’ve been having these awful dreams—reliving the accident, over and over. I’m back in the car, skidding on black ice, the headlights coming right at me… I wake up gasping, heart pounding like I’m still in it. It’s happening almost every night now. During the day, sometimes out of nowhere, I’ll get hit with this wave—like I’m not really here. Just for a few seconds. Last week, I was reviewing an employee’s file, and suddenly I wasn’t in the office anymore. I could smell gasoline, feel the steering wheel jerk. It passed quickly, but my hands were shaking. My husband says I’ve been distant, like I’m somewhere else even when I’m right beside him. I snap at the kids over little things—stuff I’d never react to before. I don’t want to get in a car anymore, but I have to. I’m managing work, just barely, but I can’t focus like I used to. It’s only been a few weeks—maybe three? I keep thinking I should just pull myself together, but it doesn’t feel like something I can just “get over.” I don’t know if it’s getting better or worse. Some days feel normal. Others… it’s like the whole thing just resets.

A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D019-D018_h006.question:
I’ve been waking up every morning around 4 a.m., even when I’m exhausted. The lights aren’t on yet, and the studio doesn’t open for hours—there’s just silence, but I can’t go back to sleep. It’s like my body’s stuck in overdrive.  

Three weeks ago, something happened… I don’t talk about it, but it’s changed everything. I remember pieces—the flashing lights, the way my shoes slipped on the wet floor—but there’s a chunk of time I can’t access, like it’s been erased. I know I was found near the stage door, but I don’t remember how I got there.  

Dancing used to make me feel alive. Now, when I perform, it’s like I’m watching myself from the ceiling. Joy, fear, sadness—they’re all muffled, like there’s a wall between me and the world. I smile during curtain calls, but inside, it’s hollow. My director asked if I’m okay, but how do I explain that I feel like I’m disappearing?  

Some days feel clearer than others, but I don’t know if this is just… shock, or something more. I keep waiting to feel like myself again—but she hasn’t come back yet.
D019-D018_h006.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D018_h006.answer: D & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h007.question:
I’ve been having a hard time sleeping lately—like, I’ll wake up around three, four in the morning, and my mind just races. No matter how tired I am, I can’t get back to sleep. It’s been happening off and on, but more often since… well, since that incident on the line.  

I remember seeing him on the tracks too late to stop the train. I can picture the lights, the platform, even the sound of the brakes—but there’s a chunk right in the middle I can’t access, like a gap in a tape. I remember before, I remember after, but not… him. Not exactly what happened in that second.  

My wife keeps trying to cheer me up—she took me to that diner I used to love, you know, the one with the terrible coffee and the jukebox—and I just sat there. I wanted to feel something. I knew I *should* be happy, sitting across from her, laughing at old songs, but nothing came. It was like watching myself from outside.  

Work’s been quiet since then. They gave me a few days off, but I don’t know if I’m ready. Or if I’ll ever be. Every time I close my eyes, I hear the warning chime.  

I don’t know how long this has been going on. A couple of weeks? Maybe less. I just… don’t know what’s wrong with me.
D019-D018_h007.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D018_h007.answer: D & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h008.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time sleeping—waking up two, three times a night, sometimes over little noises my husband doesn’t even hear. It feels like my brain won’t shut off, and when I do drift off, I’m jolted back awake, heart racing. I can’t explain it fully, but there are moments from… that night… that just aren’t there. Like chunks are missing. I remember getting in the car, the rain, the headlights—then suddenly I’m in the ER, but the crash itself? It’s like a gap. I can’t piece it together, no matter how hard I try.

And my husband… I love him, I know I do, but lately, it’s like I can’t *feel* it. He’ll touch my hand or say something sweet, and I just go blank inside. It scares me. I used to find comfort in small things—his voice, our routines—but now everything feels muted, distant. I don’t know if I’m just tired from work or… something more. I’ve only been this way for a *while*—I can’t even say exactly how long. Time feels blurry.

A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D018_h008.answer: D & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h009.question:
Lately, I just can’t shake this heaviness. I wake up after eight hours of sleep and feel like I haven’t rested at all—my body’s tired, my mind’s foggy, like I’m moving through water. It’s been happening since… well, since *it* happened. I don’t even know how to talk about it without my chest tightening. Whole chunks are just gone. I remember pieces—lights, yelling—but most of it? A blank. It’s not that I don’t want to remember. I *can’t*.  

I used to find joy in little things—finishing a good article, coffee on the porch, hearing from an old friend. Now? Nothing lands. Good news, bad news—it’s all the same flat hum. My editor sent me praise yesterday for a piece I wrote, and I just stared at the email, numb.  

I’ve tried working, but focus is hard. I’m home most days, avoiding calls. I’m not sure how long it’s been—weeks, maybe? I stopped tracking. Some mornings I feel almost okay, then a sound or smell shuts me down. I don’t know if this is supposed to last this long. I just know I’m not myself.

    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h010.question:
Lately, I just feel… empty. I work with patients nearing the end, and it’s always been hard, but about a while back—something shifted. I can’t even tell you exactly when, only that one day everything started feeling muffled, like I was watching my life through glass. I keep having the same dream—I’m in a patient’s room, but it’s not like any room I’ve actually been in. I can’t see their face, just their hand slipping out of mine, and I wake up gasping, heart racing. It happens almost every night now.

There’s a gap, too. I remember being called in for an emergency, but after that—nothing. Just pieces. I know I was there, but I can’t replay it, no matter how hard I try. My coworkers said I handled it well, but I don’t remember any of it.

The worst part? Nothing brings me joy anymore. My daughter made me a drawing last week—she was so proud—and I smiled, I told her it was beautiful, but inside… nothing. Just hollow. I don’t know if it’s the job, or that night, or both. I can’t tell if this has been weeks… or longer. Time’s just blurry.

    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling really off since… well, I don’t know exactly how long. A few weeks, maybe? Less than a month, I think. I can’t bring myself to say it’s been long enough to count. Ever since that incident with the robbery at the office—I was there when it happened—I just haven’t been the same.  

Now, I stare at my closet every morning and can’t decide what to wear. It sounds silly, I know, but nothing feels *right*, and I keep second-guessing myself. At lunch, I can’t pick what to eat—even the salad bar overwhelms me. My husband notices. He says I’ve been jumpy, distant.  

I find myself watching the doors whenever I’m out—restaurants, the grocery store—always checking who’s coming in, if someone moves too fast. If someone walks up behind me suddenly, I flinch hard, sometimes gasp. It’s embarrassing. My coworker tried to tap my shoulder last week and I nearly stood up from my chair.  

I keep thinking it could happen again—something like that. Not all the time, but enough that I’m never quite relaxed. I don’t know if this is just stress or something more. It hasn’t been *that* long… has it?

    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h012.question:
I’ve been on edge for… I don’t even know how long exactly—weeks, maybe? Feels like my body won’t shut off, like I’m always waiting for something bad to happen, even at home on the couch, lights on, nothing going on. My wife keeps asking why I jump every time she walks into the room, and I can’t explain it—just sudden movement, even if it’s her, and I flinch like I’ve been caught. 

At work, it’s getting worse. I used to make calls, assign shifts, no problem. Now I stand there second-guessing everything—what to say, who to assign, even what to have for lunch. It sounds dumb, but I’ll stare at the cafeteria menu like I can’t read the words. My hands won’t stop shaking, not violently, but enough that I hide them. 

I keep replaying that day… I mean, I know it happened, and it hit hard, but I won’t say it’s *changed* me, not permanently. It’s just… I can’t settle. Even when I’m safe. Even when there’s no reason. I’m alert all the time, like my body forgot how to relax. But is it still just the shock of it? Or has it become something else? I can’t tell the difference.
D019-D018_h012.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h013.question:
I’ve just been... off since it happened. I can’t settle, no matter where I am—even at home, even with my husband right there. It’s like my body won’t let me relax. I’ll be in the middle of planning a client’s seating chart or going over contracts, and my mind just blanks. I’ll read the same sentence three times and still not know what it says. Conversations slip past me; people have to repeat themselves, and I hate that they notice.  

I’m always watching—at work, at the grocery store, even when I’m driving. If someone walks too quickly behind me or appears suddenly around a corner, I jump. Last week, a bridesmaid opened a door right as I was passing, and I actually gasped, stepped back—it was embarrassing. I keep thinking something’s about to go wrong, even when everything’s fine.  

It hasn’t been that long—maybe a couple of weeks? I try not to count. I thought I’d be over it by now. Some days I feel okay, and then something small sets me off, and I’m right back in that tight, wired feeling. I don’t know if this is just grief, or shock, or if it’s going to last. I just know I can’t focus, I can’t rest, and I keep waiting for the next bad thing to happen.
D019-D018_h013.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D018_h014.question:

D019-D018_h015.question:

It’s not like it happens every second, but the alertness never really goes away. Like I’m wired to catch danger before it hits. I don’t know if this is normal or if I should be over it by now. D019-D018_h016.question:
I’ve been off ever since it happened. I can’t drive past the intersection where the accident took place—just seeing that stretch of road makes my chest tighten and my hands sweat, even if I’m not the one driving. Others, a sound—like screeching tires or a slamming door—and I’m right back there, or at least partway.

It’s only been… I don’t know, a few weeks? Maybe less. Time’s been blurry. I don’t know if I’m overreacting or if this is normal. I just know I can’t go back to that place, and I can’t remember what happened—even though part of me feels like I should.

D019-D018_h017.question:

The thing is, I remember bits of that night really clearly—the streetlight flickering, the sound of glass cracking—but then… nothing for a stretch. Like a missing panel in a comic. I know something happened, but I can’t pull it back no matter how hard I try. I haven’t told anyone, and I haven’t gone back to that part of the city. I don’t know if I ever will. D019-D018_h018.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—reliving the same night, over and over. It’s always the same details: the cracked streetlight, the sound of breaking glass, the way the air felt so still right before everything happened. Memories flood in, but it’s weird—some parts are crystal clear, like her red scarf on the pavement. But other pieces? Like what she said right after, or how long we stood there—gone. I can’t pull them back, no matter how hard I try.

I don’t know if I’m just stressed or if this is something worse. Some weeks I feel okay, other weeks it’s like I’m drowning. I haven’t told anyone. I just try to keep moving. I don’t even know how long it’s been now—weeks? A couple months? Time’s been blurry since that night.

D019-D018_h019.question:
I’ve been having a hard time since… well, since the accident. I don’t like to talk about it, but it was bad—real bad. Sometimes, just the sound of a loud clang, like pots dropping in the kitchen, and I freeze up. My chest gets tight, my hands shake, like I’m right back there. And truth is… I can’t remember much. Whole pieces are just gone. I know the police said my car was totaled, but last thing I clearly recall is leaving work. After that? Fog. I wake up in a hospital bed, no idea how I got there. I try not to think about it. Talking helps, I guess, but some days, I just can’t. It’s like my mind shuts the door.

D019-D018_h020.question:

I’ve been having these dreams—over and over—where I’m back in that burning building. I can smell the smoke, hear the alarms, feel the heat on my face. I wake up sweating, heart pounding, like I just barely escaped. It’s always the same. I don’t know how long this has been going on—weeks, maybe? I used to sleep fine.

I keep thinking about it during the day. Little things trigger it: a siren outside, someone mentioning fire drills. I avoid watching news clips about accidents. I don’t know if I’m overreacting, but it feels like my mind won’t let it go. I used to handle stress better.  

I haven’t told anyone about the dreams. I just... can’t find the right time. Sometimes I wonder if it’ll just fade on its own. I don’t even know when it really started—time’s been blurry.

D019-D018_h024.question:
I’ve been a security guard at the warehouse for twelve years—nothing much ever happened, or at least nothing I couldn’t handle. But about a few weeks back, I responded to a break-in alarm during my shift. It turned violent—a guy had a knife, came at me. I managed to subdue him until the police came, but… I haven’t been the same since.

I keep seeing flashes of that knife, even when I’m sitting at home watching TV. If someone slams a door too hard, my chest goes tight, my heart starts racing like I’m back there. My wife says I flinch at nothing. And the anger—God, I didn’t used to be like this. Last weekend, I yelled at my grandson for spilling juice, really tore into him. I felt awful after, but in the moment, it was like something snapped.

I don’t know how long this’ll last. Some days are okay. Others, I feel wired, on edge like I’m still on patrol. I haven’t missed work, but I don’t want to talk about it. I just hope it passes. I haven’t been able to sleep through the night since it happened—maybe a few times. But I wouldn’t say it’s every day. It’s… spotty.
